H1.verified: The in-process archive build is replaced by package_export_worker.main in the A4 owned transient unit, with m10-export prefix, export FSIZE/runtime limits and reused cgroup/seccomp/NoNewPrivs/Landlock confinement. The launcher waits for cleanup on cancellation. Source confinement is present, and the shared A4 defaults remain intact.
H1.remaining: The worker consumes mutable pathnames rather than the host-pinned snapshot/output inodes (N1). builder_identity_digest records bytes before snapshotting but neither the launcher nor worker checks that the file actually loaded still matches that digest; the separately loaded quality_probe_worker.py is not included in that export identity. Export does not use the A4 control_identity_digest/report verification path. The stdout report is accepted without checking its schema, envelope or Landlock identity. Real confined-worker/network/runtime enforcement is builder-supplied evidence, not reviewer execution. Close the path/identity and outcome gaps before declaring the complete D7 boundary closed.

A swapped work-directory ancestor can redirect its Landlock grant and output open away from the host-pinned inode. N1 was reproduced using the actual Landlock helper. open_export_store also opens project_root as one pathname: its O_NOFOLLOW protects the final component, not every ancestor as its docstring claims; no arbitrary trusted-root completeness claim is made.

M2.verified: plan_export claims every normalized case-folded destination before insertion. Primary metadata is claimed first; metadata and en/EN collisions raise instead of overwriting. Localized documents are a sequence rather than a lossy dict. Source and regression cases match the requested refusal; PG execution was unavailable to reviewer.

M3.verified: A successfully constructed work directory owns all snapshots/partial output; export finally removes it on normal failure and cancellation after launch cleanup. Known scripted refusal and unknown same-command refusal tests were added. _publish maps rename/fsync OSError to a typed integrity error.
M3.remaining: Constructor failure occurs before the export try/finally and leaks resources/orphans (N5). Supervisor exceptions and unverified cleanup can still become ordinary FAILED_BEFORE_ACCEPTANCE (N3). ENVELOPE_EXCEEDED is raised inside the callback, but _submit and _resume map every FAILED_BEFORE_ACCEPTANCE to ExportIntegrityFailedError, losing the original typed envelope refusal. Persisted ENOSPC/fsync/rename and before/after-publication failure tests remain absent.

M4.verified: The sweep skips a held owner.lock and skips work directories without an owner.lock. The stable held-lock versus orphan regression passed freshly.
M4.remaining: owner.lock becomes visible at os.open before the creator takes flock. A sweep in that window takes the lock and removes the live directory; then the creator flocks an unlinked inode and its next create fails. A deterministic boundary probe reproduced this. Serialize directory/owner-lock publication with the sweep, or publish an already-owned directory atomically. Owner-process death also does not prove a separately owned worker unit has stopped; qualify sweep policy against that lifecycle rather than claiming every free flock proves no export is running.

M5.verified: The plan is computed before opening scratch/copying media and before PLANNED. Exact ZIP headers/central-directory/manifest bytes, member-count cap and the zipfile 1.05 member-size margin are included. Golden/exact-size/no-ZIP64 tests passed. A 2,100,000,000-byte member now produces OperationalEnvelopeExceededError before copying.
M5.remaining: A payload closure over the contract sum cap fails ExportManifest validation and is translated to ExportIntegrityFailedError, bypassing the operational-envelope handler. An individual entry over the contract cap can raise Pydantic ValidationError outside the try block. Probes of a 2,147,483,647-byte video plus metadata and two 1.2GB assets returned ExportIntegrityFailedError, not the required OperationalEnvelopeExceededError. Preflight also omits the actual reused confinement config path-count cap (N4).

M7.verified: Stored request_json and selection_id are compared to the supplied request. Finalize recomputes execution_identity_digest, compares the attempt task id, reads the accepted job digest, verifies the ZIP outside locks, then rechecks the named file generation and currentness before atomic SUCCEEDED/receipt. It now compares member names, selected fixed fields, declared sizes and exact embedded manifest bytes.
M7.remaining: verify_archive never hashes/decompresses the non-manifest member bytes against ExportManifestEntry.content_digest (or even checks their CRCs). A real ZIP declaring good in the embedded manifest but containing evil was accepted by the actual verifier. It also omits several frozen ZipInfo checks (create_system, create_version, extract_version, flag_bits, member comment). execution_identity_digest does not assert that manifest.slot/selection_id/selection_digest match request.subject, and finalize does not compare the reconstructed provider request digest or route to the M7 attempt. Comparing the stored task id to the attempt task id does not prove either equals export_task_id of this command. Finally generation excludes ctime and can be preserved across a rewrite (N2). Add semantic member verification and full request/manifest/task/route/attempt cross-binding refusals, not just self-consistent cached digest comparisons.

L1.verified: The standalone writer now validates the complete lowercase normalized grammar, explicit NUL and reserved-manifest rejection, and uniqueness before destination creation. Uppercase, dot/double-separator, backslash, colon, space and NUL vectors passed. Golden bytes are preserved. The case-collision-named test actually duplicates an identical lowercase path; uppercase is independently rejected by grammar, so this does not leave an identified implementation defect.

M.title: Worker scratch confinement re-resolves mutable paths instead of the host-pinned inodes
M.scenario: After WorkDirectory pins its directory descriptor, replace its named path with a symlink to a sibling outside directory containing an empty archive.partial. The host retains the original empty output inode, but the worker config still names work.path/archive.partial. The actual A4 install_landlock uses O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW only on the final component, so its rule grants the outside regular inode through the symlink ancestor; the worker reopens that same outside path with O_NOFOLLOW and writes it. A child-process probe installed real Landlock ABI 8, successfully wrote outside-written-after-landlock into the outside file, and left the host-pinned original output empty. Host-side postverification may fail, but the outside write has already occurred. The probe exercises real Landlock path resolution, not a full systemd/cgroup launch.
M.fix: Make the worker receive the exact verified snapshot/output inode identities through a secure descriptor or private mount/namespace handoff. Do not rebuild the authority boundary from mutable project paths. At minimum perform descriptor-relative ancestor traversal and bind/open/revalidate the same exact inodes, retaining them across confinement and writing; account for confine closing inherited descriptors. Add a raced work-directory/exports ancestor swap regression proving zero outside writes and that the worker output is the host-pinned inode. This is the residual M1/D7 boundary, not another claim that host _publish follows destination links.

M.title: The generation recheck accepts a same-size rewrite with restored mtime
M.scenario: VerifiedArchive.generation contains only dev, inode, size and mtime_ns. After verification, overwrite bytes in the same inode without changing length and restore mtime with os.utime. The final published_generation check returns the previous tuple although content changed. The live probe confirmed generation equality and a changed ctime. Thus the metadata transaction can receipt bytes different from the verified digest without a SHA256 collision.
M.fix: Include at least ctime_ns in the generation and retain a verified file descriptor. Establish an enforced publication immutability or mutation-fencing boundary through final acceptance, rather than relying solely on mutable metadata; descriptor identity alone does not freeze bytes. Add a deterministic rewrite-between-verify-and-final-stat regression preserving size/mtime and assert no SUCCEEDED/receipt.

M.title: Unverified cleanup and supervisor exceptions can be committed as definite failures
M.scenario: INTEGRITY_FAILED/ENVELOPE_EXCEEDED reports are handled before exit/manager/group-cleanup validation. A fake outcome with group_cleanup_verified=False and INTEGRITY_FAILED escaped as ExportIntegrityFailedError. A RuntimeError raised by launch after a possible worker start escaped unwrapped. The real M7 service classifies every ordinary Exception as FAILED_BEFORE_ACCEPTANCE; only AmbiguousSubmitError yields SUBMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. The caller then removes scratch even when worker cleanup is unverified. Neither case is the D7 promise that all other worker outcomes remain unknown.
M.fix: Validate the full expected report schema and supervisor/cleanup evidence before treating a refusal as known. Catch unexpected exceptions after possible worker start and map them to AmbiguousSubmitError, preserving only demonstrably known startup/build/publication failures. Keep scratch ownership until worker termination is established, and retain/replay typed known failure evidence where required. Add cleanup-false known-status and supervisor-exception-after-start tests that assert UNKNOWN, no same-command rebuild and safe scratch lifetime.

M.title: Plan admission ignores the reused confinement configuration limits
M.scenario: The reused A4 _paths rejects more than 64 read_files. Export appends READ_FILES, manifest.bytes and every asset/document. A plan with 64 localized documents was accepted with 65 document members, 68 read paths and a roughly 1MB archive; the exact _paths helper then rejected it with CONFIG_INVALID. On the real route this happens only after PLANNED, inside confine; main converts it to WORKER_FAILED and the command becomes UNKNOWN. The ZIP preflight permits up to 65,535 entries, and no candidate localization count cap reconciles that with the reused worker limit. The worker also reads at most 1MiB of JSON config without export-side serialized-config admission.
M.fix: Validate the actual export worker config envelope before snapshots and PLANNED, including all path counts and serialized configuration bytes. Either explicitly support an export-specific bounded path count in the shared helper or refuse excess with OperationalEnvelopeExceededError during planning. Persist exact boundary tests (64/65 total read paths and max config bytes) asserting zero invocation/attempt on refusal.

M.title: Work-directory initialization failures leak descriptors and unsweepable scratch
M.scenario: WorkDirectory opens its directory before creating owner.lock, but constructor failure has no rollback. export obtains the store and constructs WorkDirectory before entering its try/finally. Injecting ENOSPC at owner.lock creation for three constructors leaked three directory descriptors and left three lockless work directories; sweep_work removed zero because it deliberately skips lockless directories. The full export path additionally leaves its store descriptor open when construction raises. Repeated failures can exhaust server descriptors during an existing disk-full incident.
M.fix: Make WorkDirectory construction exception-safe: close partially acquired descriptors and remove any newly created directory if ownership initialization fails. Put store ownership under an outer try/finally before invoking the constructor. Resolve this together with the atomic lock-publication/sweep protocol in M4, and persist ENOSPC/failure-at-each-acquisition tests asserting stable FD counts and no abandoned work directories.
